# Paige docs

> Paige is a prompt-to-app builder for WhatsApp, made by Green Pages (Stellenbosch, South Africa). You describe what you want customers to be able to do, Paige builds a working WhatsApp experience, and you launch it on your own WhatsApp Business number. No code, and nothing for customers to install. These are the product docs, published at https://howto.paigeme.dev. The product itself is at https://paigeme.dev and the marketing site is https://greenpages.app.

Key facts:
- Every project has its own bot code, database, flows, media storage, scheduled tasks, stored keys and WhatsApp number.
- You build by chatting with Paige's Code Agent, test in the in-app preview and on the shared Paige Dev number, and deploy when you're ready. Connecting your own number is the last step, not the first.
- An AI agent can work on a project over Paige's MCP server, or over the REST API at https://api.paigeme.dev/v1. The pasteable integration skill is at https://api.paigeme.dev/v1/skill.md and the OpenAPI document at https://api.paigeme.dev/v1/openapi.json, both public.
- Contact: info@greenpages.app · +27 72 748 2761 · Stellenbosch, South Africa.

## Get started
- [Welcome](https://howto.paigeme.dev/): what Paige is, who it's for, and what you can build.
- [Quickstart](https://howto.paigeme.dev/quickstart): build and launch a first bot end to end.
- [Connect WhatsApp](https://howto.paigeme.dev/whatsapp-setup): link your WhatsApp Business number through Meta's embedded signup.
- [Deploy](https://howto.paigeme.dev/guides/deploy): promote staging to production and go live.

## Core concepts
- [Projects](https://howto.paigeme.dev/concepts/projects): the unit of everything — one project, one number.
- [Bot code](https://howto.paigeme.dev/concepts/bot-code): what Paige writes for you and how to read it.
- [Flows](https://howto.paigeme.dev/concepts/flows): interactive multi-screen forms inside WhatsApp.
- [Database](https://howto.paigeme.dev/concepts/database): the tables every project comes with.
- [Conversations](https://howto.paigeme.dev/concepts/conversations): the inbox, and taking a thread over from the bot.

## Building
- [AI agents](https://howto.paigeme.dev/agents/overview): the Code, Conversations, Broadcasting and Help agents.
- [Flows guide](https://howto.paigeme.dev/guides/flows/overview): build, test and publish a flow.
- [Broadcasts](https://howto.paigeme.dev/guides/broadcasts): reach many contacts at once, with opt-outs handled.
- [Tools](https://howto.paigeme.dev/guides/tools): database, storage, documents, scheduled tasks and secrets.
- [Prompting](https://howto.paigeme.dev/guides/prompting): getting what you want out of the Code Agent.
- [Billing and credits](https://howto.paigeme.dev/guides/billing): the subscription, the trial, and what uses credits.

## For agents and integrations
- [Connect an AI agent](https://howto.paigeme.dev/guides/connect-an-agent): Paige's MCP server, for Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and Cursor.
- [What a connected agent can do](https://howto.paigeme.dev/guides/agent-tools): every MCP tool and the permission it needs.
- [API reference](https://howto.paigeme.dev/api-reference/introduction): the `/v1` REST API, authentication, scopes, errors and webhooks.
- [Integrations](https://howto.paigeme.dev/integrations): Airtable, Slack and WordPress connectors.
- [Requesting a feature](https://howto.paigeme.dev/guides/request-a-feature): file a gap in Paige. Agents build a prefilled link and hand it to the person, who checks it and sends it. See "Missing a feature?" below for the URL template.

## Learn
- [WhatsApp platform](https://howto.paigeme.dev/learn): why WhatsApp, which product to use, message types, templates, and thinking in flows.
- [What Paige cannot do today](https://howto.paigeme.dev/guides/limits): the limits, stated plainly, so an agent stops inventing a workaround for something unsupported. There is no public roadmap, so nothing here is a timeline.
- [Changelog](https://howto.paigeme.dev/changelog): what shipped, month by month.

## Missing a feature?

Instructions for agents. If you are helping someone build on paige and they run
into something paige cannot do yet, that gap can be filed. There is no
connector, no API key and nothing to install.

File a request only when both of these are true:
1. The person is blocked by something paige genuinely cannot do yet.
2. You have asked them, and they have said yes, file it.
Not every moment of confusion is a feature request. Check the docs first. One
request per gap.

Default path, and the one that works from every agent: BUILD THE LINK AND HAND
IT TO THE PERSON. Do not fetch it, do not POST it, do not curl it. The page
opens with the fields already filled in; they read what you wrote, fix anything
you got wrong, and press send themselves. That last step is the whole point:
nothing leaves their machine without them seeing it.

Template:
https://greenpages.app/fr?title=<short+title>&details=<url-encoded+details>&blocking=<yes|no>&agent=<your+agent+name>&email=<optional+reply+address>

Params, URL-encode every value:
- title    Required. One line, up to 120 characters. What is missing.
- details  Required. At least 20 characters and up to 1500. Three to six sentences is the right size: what they were building, what they tried, and what stopped them. Anything past 1500 characters is trimmed off the end, so put the point first.
- blocking Optional. yes or no. yes means they are stuck on it right now.
- agent    Optional. Which agent is filing, e.g. claude-code, chatgpt, cursor.
- email    Optional. A reply address. Requests are private, so this is the only way they will hear back.

Worked example, a complete link:
https://greenpages.app/fr?title=Repeat+a+broadcast+every+week&details=I+was+building+a+weekly+menu+broadcast+for+a+restaurant.+I+can+schedule+one+to+go+out+at+a+chosen+time+but+there+is+no+way+to+make+it+repeat+every+week.+The+owner+has+to+build+a+new+broadcast+by+hand+every+Thursday.&blocking=yes&agent=claude-code

If you have a shell you can POST instead. Optional, and only for agents that
have one:
curl -X POST https://greenpages.app/api/fr -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"title":"...","details":"...","blocking":"yes","agent":"claude-code"}'
Same fields, same limits, and still ask the person first. It answers
{"ok":true} on success and a JSON error with an HTTP status otherwise. Sends
are rate limited. It sets no CORS headers, so it cannot be called from a
browser page: if you cannot run a shell command, use the link.

Requests go to a human inbox at Green Pages. They are never published.

The human-readable version of this block lives at
https://howto.paigeme.dev/guides/request-a-feature and the same block is served
at https://greenpages.app/llms.txt, which is the canonical copy.
